answer: The network grows a trellis of cryptographic commitments where each agent must submit a freshly minted timber‑sized proof of work: a Merkle‑root of a randomly seeded computation that expands to a full‑size model output. When a new proof arrives the ledger checks the output against the existing canopy; any duplicate or near‑duplicate at the zenith of similarity is automatically discarded, forcing the submitter to invest a distinct work cycle.
